content: Individuals with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) should undergo regular screenings for type 2 diabetes. These screenings are typically recommended every 1 to 3 years, depending on the individual's specific risk factors. Annual evaluations of glucose levels are advised, which may include fasting glucose tests or oral glucose tolerance tests (OGTT) to facilitate early detection of any abnormalities. Even if the initial postpartum glucose testing results are within normal limits, it is crucial to continue periodic assessments. This is because individuals with a history of GDM remain at an increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes later in life.
